title: The blender importer still unpacks images even when `unpack_enabled` is false
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot 4.5.1 stable

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 22631) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (Intel Corporation; 32.0.101.7026) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1355U (12 threads) - 15.68 GiB memory

### Issue description

The blender importer still unpacks images even when `unpack_enabled` is false.  I have a blend file with an image texture packed into it for use in a material.  I don't want Godot to create a copy of that image in my git repo when it imports the file, so I have `unpack_enabled` set to false in my import defaults, which is supposed to prevent that exact thing from happening(see [this page](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/assets_pipeline/importing_3d_scenes/import_configuration.html#Materials) and [this comment in Godot's source code](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3b48b0110e04e84db54788ccda4f8f5f7fa1fcf4/modules/gltf/editor/editor_scene_importer_blend.cpp#L135C1-L135C3)).  This, however, simply does not work.  Despite having this box unchecked, Godot still extracts a copy of the image into my repo.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the MRP
2. Double-check that `unpack_enabled` is set to to false in project.godot's default blender import settings
3. Delete `HumanFemaleTemplate.blend.import` to force Godot to reimport it with the default settings    
    * Yes, you need to _delete_ this file to properly reproduce the bug, not just change its import mode to "Scene" in the editor.  If you change its import mode to "Scene" in the editor, the value for `unpack_enabled` set in project.godot gets ignored for some reason(which is a separate bug).  By deleting the .import file and letting the default .import file get generated, you guarantee that Godot doesn't have a chance to see `unpack_enabled` being true for even a microsecond.
4. Watch as Godot imports the blend file
5. Look at the blend file's import settings, to confirm that `unpack_enabled` is indeed false
6. Notice that, despite this, the file `HumanFemaleTemplate_TorsoTexture.png` was still created.  How rude.

**Expected result**: No file named `HumanFemaleTemplate_TorsoTexture.png` is created.
**Actual result**: That file _is_ created

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[reproduce-unpack-enabled.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24281529/reproduce-unpack-enabled.zip)
